subject.title: [Security] Session hijacking vulnerability due to predictable sequence IDs in gateway client

question: Does any supported gateway transport or client path allow a different socket to gain request or session authority solely by predicting an event `seq` value?
rationale: Current source separates event ordering from authentication, but the protected security report requires an explicit owner confirmation of the complete gateway boundary before closure.

options.title: Confirm boundary and close
options.body: Verify with a focused cross-socket test that guessed event sequence values cannot bypass connect authentication, device authorization, scopes, or socket-local dispatch, then close as not reproducible.

options.title: Request a working proof
options.body: Keep the report open and ask for a minimal packet-level proof showing the attacker prerequisites, injected frame, victim connection, and accepted unauthorized result.

options.title: Open a private advisory
options.body: If an authenticated or unauthenticated bypass is demonstrated, move reproduction and remediation details to the repository's private security process.

recommendation.title: Confirm boundary and close
recommendation.body: Verify with a focused cross-socket test that guessed event sequence values cannot bypass connect authentication, device authorization, scopes, or socket-local dispatch, then close as not reproducible.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged history is most directly tied to gateway authentication, device pairing, scope binding, and authorization hardening.
